PCC.label: Microgrid point of common coupling (PCC) breaker

bulk.title: Bulk power: gas plant + wind farm
bulk.what: Large generators connected to the high-voltage transmission system. Here they stand in for the whole bulk grid: in OpenDSS they are one strong 115 kV source.
bulk.role: Generation is far from load. Raising voltage for transmission cuts the current, and line losses scale with current squared, so high voltage is what makes distance affordable.

sub_hv.title: Substation, 115 kV side
sub_hv.what: Where the transmission line lands. Disconnect switches, breakers and instrument transformers protect and measure the incoming line.
sub_hv.role: The boundary between transmission (bulk, meshed, high voltage) and distribution (local, mostly radial, medium voltage).

sub_lv.title: Substation 12.47 kV bus
sub_lv.what: The medium-voltage bus that feeds the distribution feeders through their own breakers.
sub_lv.role: Each feeder breaker can isolate its feeder without affecting the others.

TL1.title: 115 kV transmission line
TL1.what: Overhead conductors on steel lattice towers, 14 km long.
TL1.role: Moves bulk power to the substation. Transmission lines are usually part of a meshed network, so one line can trip without dropping customers; here it is the only source, a single point of failure.

XFMR.title: Substation power transformer
XFMR.what: Steps 115 kV down to 12.47 kV. Oil-filled tank, high- and low-voltage bushings, radiators for cooling. Delta on the high side, grounded wye on the low side.
XFMR.role: The most expensive single piece of equipment in the substation. Losing it drops both feeders until a mobile transformer arrives, which is why utilities study it carefully.

BKR_F1.title: Feeder 1 circuit breaker
BKR_F1.what: A breaker that can interrupt fault current, controlled by an overcurrent protective relay.
BKR_F1.role: When a fault draws thousands of amps, the relay trips the breaker in a fraction of a second. Closing it again before the fault is isolated ("reclosing into a fault") trips it again and stresses equipment.

BKR_F2.title: Feeder 2 circuit breaker
BKR_F2.what: The same kind of breaker as Feeder 1, protecting Feeder 2.
BKR_F2.role: If Feeder 2 is ever connected to a fault (for example through the tie switch), this breaker trips and Feeder 2's customers go out too.

L1.title: Feeder 1, section 1
L1.what: Overhead 12.47 kV line on wood poles, 1.6 km.
L1.role: Carries all of Feeder 1's load, so it is the most heavily loaded section.

L2.title: Feeder 1, section 2
L2.what: Overhead 12.47 kV line, 1.8 km, between switches SW-A and SW-B.
L2.role: Because it has a switch at each end, a fault here can be isolated and the rest of the feeder restored. That's what sectionalizing is for.

L3.title: Feeder 1, section 3
L3.what: Overhead 12.47 kV line, 1.7 km, out to Lakeview.
L3.role: Feeds Lakeview and the microgrid's point of common coupling.

L5.title: Feeder 2 line
L5.what: Overhead 12.47 kV line, 2.6 km, with a smaller conductor than Feeder 1.
L5.role: Its lower rating is what limits how much of Feeder 1 can be picked up through the tie.

SW_A.title: Sectionalizing switch A
SW_A.what: A pole-top switch that can be opened and closed under load but cannot interrupt fault current.
SW_A.role: Opening it separates section L2 from the substation side.

SW_B.title: Sectionalizing switch B
SW_B.what: A pole-top load-break switch at the downstream end of section L2.
SW_B.role: Opening it separates L2 from the downstream customers, so they can be fed from elsewhere.

TIE.title: Normally-open tie switch
TIE.what: A switch between two feeders that is normally left open.
TIE.role: Feeders run radially (one source each) to keep protection simple. The tie lets operators move load from one feeder to the other during outages or maintenance. Never close a tie into an un-isolated fault.

PCC.title: Microgrid point of common coupling (PCC)
PCC.what: The breaker that connects the microgrid to the utility feeder.
PCC.role: When the grid fails it opens automatically and the microgrid islands. Reconnecting needs a sync check: grid voltage must be present and match the island's voltage and frequency.

mg.title: Microgrid campus
mg.what: A hospital, a water treatment plant and a fire station with their own solar and battery.
mg.role: A microgrid can disconnect and keep its critical loads running from local resources, then reconnect and support the grid when it returns.
mg.nameplate: 0.9 MW critical load, 0.8 MW PV, 2 MW / 8 MWh battery

bess.title: Battery energy storage system (BESS)
bess.what: Lithium-ion battery containers with grid-forming inverters.
bess.role: Grid-connected, it follows a dispatch (charge from midday solar, discharge at peak or to relieve a feeder). Islanded, it is grid-forming: it sets the voltage and frequency that everything else in the microgrid follows.

pv_farm.title: Solar Ridge solar farm
pv_farm.what: Ground-mounted PV arrays with inverters, on Feeder 2.
pv_farm.role: Output follows the sun and drops quickly under clouds. On a sunny afternoon it can push power back toward the substation (reverse flow).

pv_mg.title: Microgrid solar
pv_mg.what: Rooftop and carport PV on the campus.
pv_mg.role: Reduces what the battery must supply when islanded.

fci.title: Fault circuit indicators (FCIs)
fci.what: Small sensors clamped on the line that flag (here: orange) when fault current passes.
fci.role: Crews and operators follow the flags: the fault is past the last flagged device. That turns hours of patrolling into minutes.
